title: Insider PowerToys version tricks the Microsoft store into thinking that PowerToys is not installed
author: ReginaldTang
summary: After moving to an Insider PowerToys build, Microsoft Store no longer recognizes the installed application and offers installation instead of an update.

status.label: Store identity reproduction ready
status.detail: The report identifies a specific stable-to-Insider transition that maintainers can verify without asking for generic diagnostics first.

next_action.label: Reproduce Store registration transition
next_action.reason: Determine whether the Insider installation changes package identity or Store ownership recognition.

judgment.rationale: The installation-channel transition and Store symptom are concrete enough for a controlled maintainer reproduction. The result will distinguish an expected preview-channel limitation from a packaging identity regression.
evidence: The report describes installing an Insider PowerToys version over an existing Store-recognized installation.
Microsoft Store subsequently presents PowerToys as not installed.
No assignee, duplicate, or linked fix is present.
judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce the stable Store to Insider transition and compare package registration and Store update behavior.

issue_context.summary: Microsoft Store loses recognition of PowerToys after the installation is moved to an Insider build.
known_information: The symptom follows installation of an Insider PowerToys version.
Microsoft Store offers installation rather than recognizing the existing PowerToys installation.
inferences: The Insider package may use registration or version metadata that the Store does not associate with the installed stable product.
The behavior may also be an intentional preview-channel limitation; a controlled transition will distinguish that from a defect.
issue_context.analysis: The report contains a testable channel transition. Maintainer reproduction is more useful than a broad information request because package identity and Store state can be captured directly before and after the transition.
initial_investigation: Reviewed the complete issue, labels, assignees, and timeline.
No existing maintainer response or linked remediation is present.

reproduce.version_requirements: Begin with the current Store stable release, then install the current Insider build.
prerequisites: A Windows test environment with Microsoft Store access.
steps: Install PowerToys from Microsoft Store and confirm it is recognized.
Install the current Insider build over it.
Restart Microsoft Store and open the PowerToys page.
Check whether the Store recognizes the product or offers a fresh installation.
Compare registered package/product identity before and after.
reproduce.expected_result: The Store should continue to recognize PowerToys, or an intentional preview-channel limitation should be confirmed and documented.
setup_requirements: Record installer type, architecture, stable version, Insider version, and package identity.
